title: Milestone planning: six months, one year and five years
audience: Owners of small Australian property trade businesses who want a private plan to check progress against
learningOutcomes: Write milestones for six months, one year and five years, each with a measure that can be checked from records.
Answer the planning questions on clients, time, admin, travel and hiring in writing.
Review the milestones on a fixed schedule, and record any change together with its reason.

instruction.heading: Why plan in milestones
instruction.body: Many owners start because they want more control over their work, better returns for their hours or the freedom to choose their clients. Those reasons can carry an owner through the early period, but the daily demands of running a business can wear them down. A written set of milestones gives a fixed reference point. It shows whether the business is moving toward what the owner wants, and it signals when a change of course is needed. A milestone plan is a private planning tool. It is different from a formal business plan for a lender, which needs more financial detail. “How a cleaning business plan is structured” sets out the structure of a formal plan.

instruction.heading: Setting three milestones with checkable measures
instruction.body: Describe what the business looks like at six months, at one year and at five years. Each description should contain something you could check: the number of repeat clients served, the share of enquiries answered within a set time, the share of work that comes from referrals, the hours worked on site each week, whether a team member is employed, and what the records show. Avoid phrases such as doing well or growing strongly. A measure you cannot check tells you nothing about whether you are on track.

instruction.heading: Answering the planning questions
instruction.body: Use these questions to test the milestones. How many fresh clients must come in each month, and how many existing clients can you keep? What will you spend each month on tools and their upkeep? How many hours each week will admin take? What is the longest travel time you will accept for a job? Which sources will bring in the bulk of the work? At what point will the first team member join, and when will a second follow? Keep the answers realistic. A plan that assumes a large number of new clients in six months needs strong evidence for that claim. Also write down what you want the business to be after five years: a small operation, a larger team, or a business you eventually hand to someone else.

instruction.heading: Keeping the plan honest and reviewing it
instruction.body: Review the milestones on a fixed date each quarter, and record what has changed and why. Small adjustments are normal. Frequent large changes suggest the original numbers were not based on evidence, and then the plan needs a fresh look at the demand evidence from “Choosing your service list and checking local demand” and the cash position from “Start-up costs, cash runway and business banking”. Keep the plan to one or two pages, so it stays readable and gets used.

procedure: Write one short description of the business at six months, one year and five years.
Attach at least one measure to each milestone that can be checked from the business records.
Answer the seven planning questions in writing, with a number or a time where possible.
Compare the answers with the demand evidence and the cash runway from the earlier lessons.
Mark any answer that depends on evidence you do not yet have as an assumption, and adjust it.
Set a quarterly review date, and record the date of the next check.

workedExamples.situation: An owner plans to hire a first team member at month nine. The records show a few regular clients, no spare capacity and a cash buffer that covers only a short period.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the hiring milestone stay at month nine?
workedExamples.reasoning: A hiring milestone depends on steady work and enough cash to pay wages and on-costs. With few regular clients and no spare capacity, month nine is an assumption, not a plan. The owner should move the milestone to the point where the records show consistent demand and a cash buffer, and keep the earlier date marked as a target to review.

equipmentAndPpe: Milestone plan document of one or two pages
Business records from the last quarter

commonErrors.error: Setting milestones that cannot be measured, such as growing well.
commonErrors.prevention: Attach a count, a time or a record to every milestone.

commonErrors.error: Changing the milestones every week as results come in.
commonErrors.prevention: Review on a fixed quarterly date, and record each change with its reason.

commonErrors.error: Using the milestone plan as the financial plan a lender will receive.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep this plan private, and prepare a separate formal plan when a lender asks for one.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A milestone that includes hiring brings legal obligations for pay, leave, superannuation, workers compensation and work health and safety. Those points are covered in “Deciding on your first team member” and “Setting up your first employee: cover, pay, schedule and feedback”.

qualityStandard: Each of the three milestones includes at least one measure that can be checked from records.
All seven planning questions are answered, and each assumption is marked as an assumption.
A quarterly review date is set and recorded.
documentationEvidence: Milestone plan with three dated stages and their measures
Written answers to the seven planning questions
Quarterly review log with the date and any change made
summary: Write milestones with measures that can be checked.
Test every milestone against the demand evidence and the cash position.
Review quarterly, and record why anything changed.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which milestone description is most useful for tracking progress?
options: The business will be doing well by the end of the second year
The business will grow and the owner will hire two staff
Half of new enquiries will be answered within the set response time
The owner will feel more in control and less stressed about the work

knowledgeChecks.question: A milestone depends on hiring at month nine, but the records show no spare capacity. What is the right response?
options: Keep the date, because the plan is the plan and nobody will question the date once it is written down in the plan for the bank
Move the milestone to when the records show steady demand and a cash buffer, and keep the earlier date marked as an assumption to review
Hire at month nine and find the work afterwards even if the records show no spare capacity at all and the cash is tight
Delete the milestone, because the hiring cost is already covered by the margin and the margin is never checked again

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the milestone plan be kept separate from a lender's business plan?
options: Lenders do not accept written plans and they never read any figures in a plan at all
The milestone plan is a private planning tool and needs less financial detail than a formal plan
The milestone plan must contain the bank account number and the owner's home address
A lender's plan is the shorter of the two, so it can be reused for staff and it needs no figures
